rounds.q: How many arms does a typical snowflake have?
rounds.why: Needle-like crystals form near 23 degrees F, and very flat plates form near 5 degrees F.
rounds.fun: Six arms on a classic flake. Needles form near 23 degrees and flat plates near 5!

rounds.q: What % of US homes use electricity as their main heat?
rounds.why: Natural gas still leads at 47% of homes, down from 49% in 2010.
rounds.src: US Energy Information Administration, from Census American Community Survey (2024 data)
rounds.fun: Electric heat warms 42% of homes, just 5 points behind natural gas.

rounds.q: About what % of Americans live where it snows over 5 inches a year?
rounds.why: Over 70% of US roads are in those snowy regions too.
rounds.src: Federal Highway Administration, Road Weather Management: Snow and Ice (current page, read 2026)
rounds.fun: Nearly 70% of us live in snow country, and so do most of our roads.

rounds.q: On average in the US, how many inches of snow equal 1 inch of rain?
rounds.why: It can take nearly 50 inches of very dry, powdery snow to equal that same inch of rain.
rounds.src: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Severe Weather 101: Winter Weather FAQ (current page, read 2026)
rounds.fun: Thirteen inches of fluff for one inch of rain. Dry powder can need nearly 50!

rounds.q: How many feet tall is the tallest snowman in Guinness World Records?
rounds.why: It was a snow woman, 122 ft 1 in tall, built over one month in Bethel, Maine in 2008.
rounds.src: Guinness World Records, Tallest snowperson (2008 record)
rounds.fun: A 122-foot snow woman took Bethel, Maine a whole month to build.
